289909815.heading: Have you heard of the term “child’s rights” before?
options: Can you name any of them?

289909818.heading: Please select the option that best reflects your experience or observations.
rows: How often are children in your area invited to share their views on local issues (e.g. school projects)
How often do you listen to your child’s opinions or feelings when they share them?
How often do you respond to and discuss your child’s opinions or concerns when they share them?

289909819.heading: What do you think prevents children from expressing their opinions freely? (tick all that apply)
options: Children are afraid of getting into trouble
Cultural norms that discourage children from speaking up
Fear of being judged or bullied
Lack of safe spaces to speak (at home, school or community)
Children do not know their rights
Adults do not take children’s views seriously

289909820.heading: Does your child take part in any activities outside of school? (tick all that apply)
options: Uniformed bodies (e.g., Scouts, Girl Guides, Cadet Corps)

289909821.heading: All children in my area have fair access to these kinds of activities.

289909823.heading: What are the main barriers preventing children from joining community or extracurricular activities? (tick all that apply)
options: Cost of activities (fees, equipment, uniforms, transport)
Lack of time due to schoolwork or tuition
Activities are too far from home/transport difficulties
Activities are not inclusive for children with disabilities
Lack of information about available activities

289909825.heading: There are enough public spaces (e.g. playgrounds, parks, sports areas) for children nearby.

289909826.heading: Public spaces in my area (e.g. playgrounds, parks, sports areas) could be improved by:
options: Adding more shade (e.g. trees, covered areas)
Repairing or upgrading equipment and facilities
Adding more things for young people to do
Making them easier and safer to access (e.g. crossings, walkways)
Providing more seating for families and caregivers
Reducing smoking, vaping, alcohol or drug activity
Organising more community activities or events

289909827.heading: How often does your family visit green or natural spaces (parks, beaches, gardens, forests)?

289909828.heading: To what extent do you agree with the following statements?
rows: There are safe and child-friendly paths and crossings for children in my area
There are safe and child-friendly public transport options for children in my area.

289909829.heading: How does your child get to school most days? (tick all that apply)

289909830.heading: At what age do you think it is safe to allow your child(ren) to move around your area independently?

289909831.heading: My child(ren) are safe at school from bullying, violence, or harassment.

289909832.heading: How do you keep your child(ren) safe online?
rows: I actively monitor my child(ren)’s online activity
I check which apps and platforms my child(ren) use regularly
I use parental controls or content filters on devices
I talk to my child(ren) about how to stay safe online

289909834.heading: How worried are you about climate change and its effects on your family?

289909835.heading: How is environmental change affecting your children’s daily lives? (tick all that apply)
options: More frequent illness (e.g., heat-related issues, haze, dengue)
Reduced outdoor play due to heat
School closures or disruptions (e.g., haze, flooding)
Increased household costs (e.g., cooling, medical expenses)
Travel disruptions due to flooding or extreme weather
Emotional stress or anxiety about environmental issues
Reduced outdoor play due to poor air quality

289909836.heading: Do children in your home help to protect the environment in these ways?
rows: Recycling things like paper, plastic or cans
Saving water (e.g. turning off the tap, shorter showers)
Switching off lights or fans when not in use
Using less plastic (e.g. reusable bottles or bags)
Planting trees or helping in a garden
Picking up litter or joining clean-up activities
Talking about how to protect nature or animals

289909837.heading: The authorities are doing enough to protect children from the effects of climate change?

289909840.heading: Now you will be asked about some difficulties your child may have.
rows: Does your child have difficulty seeing, even if wearing glasses?
Does your child have difficulty hearing, even if using a hearing aid?
Does your child have difficulty walking or climbing steps?
Does your child have difficulty remembering or concentrating?
Does your child have difficulty with self-care such as washing all over or dressing?
Using your usual (customary) language, does your child have difficulty communicating, for example understanding or being understood?
Compared with children of the same age, does your child have difficulty learning things?
Compared with children of the same age, does your child have difficulty controlling his/her behaviour?

289909846.heading: How much do you know about child rights?
options: I know a lot about child rights
I have heard of them but don't know much
I have never heard of them before

289909847.heading: For each question, tell us how much you agree or disagree.
rows: In my area, children are treated kindly and fairly
In my area, children are treated the same even if they are boys or girls
In my area, children are treated the same even if they have a disability

rows: I get asked for my opinion on things in my area (like school projects, community events, or local issues)?
I feel that my opinions about things in my area are listened to?

options: Using an online survey or app

I’m worried about being teased or bullied

rows: There are good indoor places for young people to go in their free time (e.g. library, youth centre)

These places welcome all young people, inc. those with disabilities or from different backgrounds
